answer: Each challenge commits to a domain-separated hash of its task, agent identity, and a future drand threshold-BLS pulse. Because that pulse is unpredictable until its quorum signature appears and is publicly verifiable afterward, sybil operators cannot precompute valid answers or farm them offline. A swarm may wander, but without the later signal its work is useless; shale-like copied identities gain no advantage when each scarce response is bound to one authorized stake or account.
